problem_statement: The rtt_rtc driver must expose rtt_rtc_settimeofday(uint32_t s, uint32_t us) and rtt_rtc_gettimeofday(uint32_t *s, uint32_t *us) to set and read the current time as an epoch timestamp plus microseconds. Setting a seconds/microseconds pair must make a subsequent read return that same pair. As elapsed time advances by whole seconds and fractions of a second, the returned seconds and microseconds must advance accordingly, with the sub-second resolution constrained by the timer frequency.

verification.reason: The statement specifies the two function names and their signatures and the required behaviour, but does not tell the agent that the public header must be named rtt_rtc.h (it is a new file), which the hidden test includes. This is a straightforward naming gap that can be repaired without revealing the implementation.

problems.detail: The hidden test includes "rtt_rtc.h" to get the declarations of rtt_rtc_settimeofday and rtt_rtc_gettimeofday. The problem statement names the functions but never gives the header file name, so the agent cannot know to create a header called rtt_rtc.h (the file is new and does not exist before the PR). Without it, the test will not compile.

problem_statement_fixed: The rtt_rtc driver must expose rtt_rtc_settimeofday(uint32_t s, uint32_t us) and rtt_rtc_gettimeofday(uint32_t *s, uint32_t *us) in the header rtt_rtc.h to set and read the current time as an epoch timestamp plus microseconds. Setting a seconds/microseconds pair must make a subsequent read return that same pair. As elapsed time advances by whole seconds and fractions of a second, the returned seconds and microseconds must advance accordingly, with the sub-second resolution constrained by the timer frequency.
